memories.content: The user renewed their local library membership in October 2024.
On an evening walk, the user saw an unlit street and took a detour along a main road.
On a day the user chose a well-lit pedestrian route, the walk took 12 minutes longer than usual.
On a day the user sat by the library window, they heard vehicle noise with every page they read.
On the next visit, the user sat farther inside and did not move for an hour.
The user wrote the due date of a borrowed book on paper and then lost the paper.
After entering the due date on their phone, the user saw a reminder the day before and put the book in their bag.
Library staff expect a person requesting a replacement membership card to bring identity-verification material.
Check recent lighting and pedestrian conditions before proposing an evening walking route.
The local agent can compare past reasons for detours but cannot directly observe current lighting and pedestrian conditions.
The user stores tax-related receipts in digital folders by year.
The user found three paper receipts late and recalculated the expense total already prepared.
Starting the next month, the user photographed receipts on the day they were received and reduced omissions.
The user named every file with only the photo date and spent a long time looking for a needed receipt.
The user later included the expense category in the filename and found the receipt immediately through search.
While reviewing documents just before submission, the user discovered one blank signature field.
Before submitting an administrative document, the user checks the signature field as the final item on the checklist.
Staff at a tax-support counter expect to receive an electronic copy in which every item is legible rather than a blurred or cropped photo.
The local agent can organize receipts by date and category but cannot determine whether an expense is deductible.
The accepted scope and submission deadlines for administrative documents may vary under that year's guidance.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate practical domains: library use and evening-route safety on the reference side, and receipt management and administrative submission on the compared side. Each contributes independent observations, practices, requirements, and capability limits; none governs the same operational decision across frames.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided historical membership event with no claim about the same matter in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user renewed a local library membership in October 2024.

relations.reason: These memories jointly supply one-sided evidence about the practical time and route costs of avoiding poorly lit pedestrian paths.
relations.summary: The user’s preference for better-lit walking routes led to a main-road detour and, on another occasion, a longer walk.

relations.reason: The memories form one one-sided sequence connecting a noisy seating location with the user’s subsequent choice of an interior seat.
relations.summary: After vehicle noise disrupted reading by a library window, the user sat farther inside on the next visit and remained there for an hour.

relations.reason: The memories split one one-sided account of replacing an ineffective paper reminder with an effective phone reminder.
relations.summary: A paper due-date note was lost, whereas entering the date on the phone produced a timely reminder and prompted the user to pack the book.

relations.reason: This one-sided service requirement has no counterpart concerning replacement library cards in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Library staff expect identity-verification material from a person requesting a replacement membership card.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided routing policy addressing current street conditions, not the administrative or receipt decisions described in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Recent lighting and pedestrian conditions should be checked before proposing an evening walking route.

relations.reason: This one-sided capability boundary is specific to evaluating evening-route conditions and does not address the compared frame’s tax-expense limitation.
relations.summary: The local agent can compare past detour reasons but cannot directly observe current lighting or pedestrian conditions.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided receipt-storage practice with no claim about the same operational matter in the reference frame.
relations.summary: The user stores tax-related receipts in digital folders organized by year.

relations.reason: The memories form one one-sided sequence linking missed paper receipts to a more reliable capture practice.
relations.summary: After late paper receipts forced recalculation, the user began photographing receipts on receipt day and reduced omissions.

relations.reason: The memories jointly describe one one-sided refinement to receipt naming and its effect on retrieval.
relations.summary: Date-only filenames made a receipt difficult to locate, while adding the expense category enabled immediate search retrieval.

relations.reason: The memories split one one-sided account of a detected omission and the resulting submission-check practice.
relations.summary: Discovering a blank signature field just before submission led to checking the signature field as the final checklist item for administrative documents.

relations.reason: This one-sided document-quality requirement has no matching claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Tax-support staff expect an electronic copy whose items are all legible rather than blurred or cropped.

relations.reason: This one-sided capability boundary concerns tax classification, a different operational decision from the reference frame’s route-observation boundary.
relations.summary: The local agent can organize receipts by date and category but cannot determine expense deductibility.

relations.reason: This is one-sided information about guidance-dependent administrative requirements and has no claim on the same matter in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Accepted scope and submission deadlines for administrative documents may vary with the applicable year’s guidance.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame describes receipt capture, storage and retrieval improvements, signature checks, electronic-copy quality, tax-related capability limits, and guidance-dependent document scope and deadlines.
reports.reference_only: The reference describes library membership, reading-location choices, due-date reminders, replacement-card requirements, and evening-route safety, including the need for current conditions beyond the local agent’s observation.
